boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Palmito Ranch record (May 12-13, 1865) in Expedition from Brazos Santiago [May 1865]. The crossing from Brazos Santiago on May 11 and the return to Boca Chica and re-embarkation on May 14 are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names detachments of the 62nd U.S. Colored Infantry, 2nd Texas Cavalry and 34th Indiana, and of Gidding's regiment, Anderson's battalion and others, without figures; the live field reads 0. Barrett and Branson give 250 of the 62nd and 50 dismounted men of the 2nd Texas Cavalry crossing on May 11, and Barrett about 200 of the 34th Indiana joining on the 13th. Branson expected an outpost of sixty-five at White's Ranch, says the Palmetto Ranch camp had held about 190 men and horses, and that the nearest enemy body in the retreat was 250 strong with two guns; Barrett says the enemy had six 12-pounder field pieces.
claims.rationale: Union column figures and opponents' estimates of parts of the Confederate force: 250 and 50 crossed on May 11; 200 joined on May 13; the outpost of sixty-five was expected on May 12; about 190 had occupied the camp before noon on May 12; the 250 with two guns and the six field pieces refer to the afternoon of May 13. No Confederate report was inspected. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.value: NPS says the expedition was sent to attack reported outposts and camps despite an informal agreement since March 1865 that precluded fighting on the Rio Grande. The inspected Union reports do not mention such an agreement; Barrett says he ordered the advance renewed toward Palmetto Ranch on the 13th, and Branson hoped to capture the White's Ranch outpost.
claims.rationale: The agreement is stated only in the NPS summary; no Confederate account was inspected.

claims.rationale: Command roles from interested Union reports and the NPS summary; no automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads US 118 and CS unknown; the live field reads 148 (US 30; CS 118), placing 118 on the Confederate side. Barrett gives his entire loss in killed, wounded and captured as 4 officers and 111 men, including 48 men of the 34th Indiana captured as skirmishers. Branson gives two men missing, and the compiler's note on his omitted list shows five wounded.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Barrett's 115 and the frozen 118 differ; the live side assignment conflicts with the frozen table.

open_questions: Any Confederate report (Ford's or Giddings's), the detailed reports Barrett says went to New Orleans, the 34th Indiana's account, returns and maps remain deferred. No third family was found in the inspected volume.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Barrett's August 10, 1865 report and Branson's May 18, 1865 report are interested Union accounts; Barrett wrote three months later, and each is a separate author family. No Confederate account was inspected. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.

No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Participants are named as the sources name them; characterizations in the sources (including 'hostile', 'savages', 'massacre' or 'battle') are quoted as the sources' own words and not adopted.
